claims.text: Al-centered short-range chemical ordering stabilizes B2-type precipitates in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni alloys.
Stabilized B2 precipitates delay detrimental phase transformations across extreme service conditions.
B2 stabilization governs retention of high-temperature strength, environmental resistance, radiation tolerance, and cryogenic toughness.
The proposed initial material is a nominally equiatomic Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni alloy.
Solution treatment will minimize pre-existing precipitates in the initial alloy.
Thermal cycling and irradiation will cause SRO-induced B2 domains to nucleate and remain stable.
SRO-induced B2 domains act as local pinning centers that hinder dislocation motion.
SRO-induced B2 domains hinder phase separation.
Al-centered chemical ordering lowers the local free energy.
Al-centered chemical ordering reduces diffusion of constituent elements.
Reduced diffusion preserves a coherent or semi-coherent B2 phase.
A coherent or semi-coherent B2 phase enhances alloy strength.
The preserved B2 phase suppresses detrimental microstructural changes under high-temperature, corrosive or oxidizing, and irradiating environments.
Relative to a lower-Al alloy, the equiatomic alloy will show more stable B2 precipitation and less phase decomposition.
Relative to a lower-Al alloy, the equiatomic alloy will develop fewer irradiation-induced defects.
Relative to a lower-Al alloy, the equiatomic alloy will retain superior mechanical properties throughout the specified temperature and irradiation range.
Excessive Al or sufficiently severe temperature or irradiation conditions may promote other intermetallics or B2 coarsening and reduce the stabilizing benefit.
Configurational entropy and kinetic constraints may contribute to phase or microstructural stability independently of Al-centered SRO.
Mechanical properties in complex concentrated alloys can correlate with short-range ordering, phase instability, and nanostructure morphology.
The hypothesis is to be rejected if stable B2 precipitates are absent or if the compared alloys show no significant property difference.
